correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.claim: "brokeragePlaceBuildableEnvelope.ts... resolves district -> ruled table -> setbacks, live in production today for ~20 jurisdictions. Use getSetbackTableForZoning from @hauska-engine/adapters. Do not write a second resolver."
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.measured: The live route's real call chain (legacy-design-tools artifacts/api-server/src/routes/brokeragePlaceBuildableEnvelope.ts -> lib/buildableEnvelope/authoritativeSetbackSource.ts:172 resolveAuthoritativeSetbacks) calls getSetbackTableForZoning from @workspace/adapters (legacy-design-tools' OWN local package, lib/adapters/src/local/setbacks/index.ts), not @hauska-engine/adapters. @hauska-engine/adapters is a separate, already-diverged fork living in a different repo (hauska-engine/packages/adapters, 3-arg signature vs. the live 2-arg one) that the live production route never calls. Neither package is published or importable cross-repo (both private, workspace-local) -- hauska-factory has no dependency path to either today.
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.evidence: legacy-design-tools lib/adapters/package.json:2 name="@workspace/adapters"; authoritativeSetbackSource.ts:172 `const table = getSetbackTableForZoning(jurisdictionKey, districtCode);`; hauska-engine packages/adapters/package.json description literally "lifted from legacy-design-tools lib/adapters per ADR-008"; hauska-engine's own copy at packages/adapters/src/local/setbacks/index.ts:152-156 has a third `options` param the live one does not.
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.consequence: the actual single published source of truth for this data is @empressaio/setback-corpus (real npm package; confirmed `npm view` versions 1.0.0/1.0.1/1.1.0, dist-tag latest=1.1.0), whose own description says it exists to replace "two independently-maintained local copies" -- but grep across both legacy-design-tools and hauska-factory finds ZERO references to it in either repo; neither has actually repointed onto it yet.
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.decisionTaken: hauska-factory (a third repo with no import path into either private package) takes @empressaio/setback-corpus as a real npm dependency for TABLE DATA, and PORTS -- not reinvents -- the small amount of consumer-side district-code routing logic (the Bastrop 3-table special case; see falsifier 2 below) verbatim from legacy-design-tools' current @workspace/adapters implementation, citing file/line at the port site. This is not "a second resolver" in the sense the dispatch prohibits (an independently-derived computation of what a district's setbacks ARE) -- same table data, same routing decisions, relocated only because the source implementation is not mechanically importable across these three repos, following the same vendor-a-trimmed-copy precedent already established for Property Explorer's own setback consumption (hauska-map PR #360).

correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.claim: "Ruled tables that exist: austin-tx, bastrop-tx, bastrop-city-tx, bastrop-development-code, elgin-development-code, kyle-tx, pflugerville-tx, round-rock-tx, san-antonio-tx, waco-tx (plus Utah/Idaho). Inside the six CTX counties that is Austin, Bastrop, Bastrop City, Elgin, Kyle, Pflugerville, Round Rock."
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.measured: This 10-table list matches legacy-design-tools' STALE, un-migrated local @workspace/adapters copy, not the published corpus. @empressaio/setback-corpus@1.1.0 ships 29 jurisdiction keys, including six more real Central Texas cities with real in-city populations inside the five in-scope counties that the dispatch's own "inside the six CTX counties" sentence omits: lockhart-tx (48055, 6,490 in-city parcels), leander-tx / cedar-park-tx / georgetown-tx / hutto-tx / taylor-tx / liberty-hill-tx (all 48491 Williamson, 91,880 in-city parcels combined), plus a tiny 7-parcel Travis sliver of buda-tx and a 72-parcel Caldwell sliver of san-marcos-tx. waco-tx itself is in the dispatch's own table list but its own city-enumeration sentence never mentions Waco/McLennan at all (48309, 48,693 in-city Waco parcels) -- an internal inconsistency in the dispatch's own two adjacent sentences.
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.evidence: npm pack @empressaio/setback-corpus@1.1.0; dist/setbacks/ contains all 29 <key>.json files. landing_parcel_jurisdiction city_name census for the 5 in-scope counties (below) cross-referenced against SETBACK_JURISDICTION_KEYS.
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.consequence: using the dispatch's named 7-city list literally would write absent-verified on ~104,780 real in-city parcels (Waco 48,693 + Lockhart 6,490 + the six Williamson cities 91,880 + slivers, minus double count adjustments) that a ruled table actually covers -- the opposite of the program's own stated goal ("values where we have data").
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.decisionTaken: derive the ruled-table city set MECHANICALLY: candidate jurisdictionKey = slugify(city_name)+"-tx", confirmed live against getSetbackTable() from the corpus (never a hand-typed list), with Bastrop and Elgin carrying the two documented special-cased keys (see falsifier 2). This is the same discipline rail-keys.js's own "do not hand-author a rail list" already applies one layer up in this program, applied here to the city list.

correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.claim: not stated in the dispatch at all -- a genuine gap, not a wrong number
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.measured: Setback resolution needs a per-parcel zoning district code as an input, which is a DIFFERENT rail (zoningDistrict) written by an already-existing, independent job (parcel-r5-zoning.mjs), not by anything in this mission's scope. Of the 288,698 in-city parcels in the dispatch's originally-named 7 ruled-table cities across the 5 in-scope counties: 287,022 (99.4%) already carry a real zoningDistrict `value`; 1,211 carry a pre-existing `not-applicable` (a cross-system disposition-timing disagreement between landing_parcel_jurisdiction's current live disposition and this cell's row-creation-time snapshot -- already internally consistent with every other UNINCORPORATED_NOT_APPLICABLE_RAIL_KEYS sibling on the same row, out of this lane's scope to reconcile); 465 (all Elgin/48453) carry a zoningDistrict `refused`.
correctionsToTheDispatchPremise.decisionTaken: read the ALREADY-WRITTEN zoningDistrict cell (same store, same place_key) as the district-code input rather than re-deriving a second spatial/staging join. A parcel whose zoningDistrict is not yet `value` stays exactly as-is this run (correctly deferred) -- except: where zoningDistrict is itself `refused`, setback cells inherit `refused` citing the upstream refusal as basis (re-probing an already-refused input would manufacture false specificity; leaving it unaccounted forever would misstate that nobody has looked, when the same source already looked and refused).

perInCityParcel: 1. Determine ruled-table jurisdictionKey for the parcel's city_name mechanically (probe @empressaio/setback-corpus's getSetbackTable). No match -> write absent-verified on all 4 scalars + setbackRules companion (empty-set), instrument='@empressaio/setback-corpus@1.1.0 getSetbackTable(<jurisdictionKey>)=null', scope=county_fips+city_name.
2. Match found (ruled-table city). Read this parcel's own zoningDistrict cell (same store, same place_key).
2a. kind=value -> route (jurisdictionKey, districtCode) through the ported router (Bastrop special-case + generic lookup, verbatim-ported from legacy-design-tools' current getSetbackTableForZoning).

- matched district -> write value cells (front_ft/side_ft/rear_ft/side_corner_ft) + setbackRules companion (rowCount 1, payload={district_name, citation_url, effective_date, note, jurisdictionKey}), source cites corpus package version + jurisdictionKey.
- no matched district (repealed code / unmapped code) -> absent-verified, instrument='ported router + corpus@1.1.0, jurisdictionKey=<k>, districtCode=<c> -> null', scope=jurisdictionKey+districtCode.
2b. kind=refused -> setback cells -> refused, instrument='zoningDistrict rail refusal for the same place_key', scope=place_key.
2c. kind=unaccounted or not-applicable or anything else -> untouched this run (correctly deferred; not-applicable case is the pre-existing cross-system drift noted above, out of lane scope).
theDesign.neverTouched: not-applicable cells (query scoped to disposition='in-city' only from the start; every UPDATE additionally guarded to cell_state->>'kind'='unaccounted', matching parcel-r5-zoning.mjs's established gated-batch-write convention -- a re-run can never regress an already-earned cell).
theDesign.placeKey: RAW county_fips:prop_id, never normalizeForJoin'd -- confirmed against parcel-r5-zoning.mjs's own buildZoningCells convention.
theDesign.writerAllowlistId: f11-setback (pre-reserved in writer-allowlist.mjs, kind='setback', planRow currently 'F-11', REQUIRED_NON_CAD_WRITERS member with no implementing job file on this branch -- this job claims it, and its planRow note is updated to also cite P-132/OPS-21-S1).
theDesign.haysExclusion: county filter hardcoded to the 5 non-Hays counties in every query this job runs; never a 6th county, honoring P-145's gate.
theDesign.companionCellShape: follows the 7-times-repeated existing companion convention ({kind:'value', disposition, rowCount, source, vintage} on the cell + one row per matched setback rule in parcel_record_companion_row.payload) rather than inventing a {value:{...}} shape on setbackRules itself -- avoids a second implementation of one meaning (DEV_PROCESS 2.4).
theDesign.deployAndApply: --apply refuses off Cloud Run (LAPTOP_WRITE_FROZEN), matching every sibling job. A cloudbuild.<job>.yaml + Cloud Run Job deploy (factory-<job>) is required before any real write; CP2's pilot is a bounded single-city --apply execution on the deployed Cloud Run job, never a local write.
